title: Suresh v. Ramesh (Property Partition)
text: A suit for partition of ancestral property. The plaintiff claims one-half share in the suit property being a co-sharer. The defendant denies the plaintiff's share alleging an oral partition. The court finds that oral partition of immovable property is not legally valid under the Transfer of Property Act. The plaintiff's share is established through the revenue records. A preliminary decree for partition and separate possession is passed. The parties are directed to appoint a court commissioner to suggest a physical division of the property. If the property cannot be equitably divided, it shall be sold by auction and proceeds divided equally. The plaintiff is entitled to half the property as co-sharer.
